programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: Archaeologist and historian Richard Miles explores the triumphs and legacy of Alexander the Great, the conqueror who rose from the kingdom of Macedon and went on to control an empire that stretched from Egypt in the West to Afghanistan in the East. The presenter also focuses on those who succeeded him after he died in Babylon, and how they tried to maintain the empire by cunning rather than by the sword

programme.title: Art of France
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon delves into how art in France took a dramatic turn after the Revolution ushered in a bold new world. He looks at the execution of Louis XVI, the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte and the ascension of Romanticism. Andrew also explores the work of artists, including Jacques-Louis David, Eugene Delacroix and Theodore Gericault

programme.title: City Lights: Pure Dead Brilliant
programme.desc: A celebration of the comedy that captured the spirit of 1980s Scotland, starring Gerard Kelly as a Glasgow bank clerk with dreams of being a best-selling author. The show's creator Bob Black and cast members Elaine C Smith, Jonathan Watson and Dave Anderson reveal their favourite moments and give behind-the-scenes insights, with bittersweet memories of co-stars Kelly and Andy Gray. With contributions from Gayle Telfer Stevens, Jordan Young, Sanjeev Kohli, Damian Barr, Johnny McKnight Kirsty Wark and Paul English

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: The story of journalist, author and advice columnist E Jean Carroll, exploring her early days as Miss Cheerleader US to how she became a pioneering voice in American magazine journalism. The programme charts her professional achievements and the legal battle against Donald Trump that brought her international attention

programme.title: 999 Special
programme.desc: Documenting the great storm of 1987, which hit the south and east of England. Michael Buerk presents reconstructions of escapes from the night the storm hit. Plus, amateur videos and news footage of the millions of pounds' worth of damage caused across the South. Including the stories of an elderly couple who survived the destruction, and a pregnant woman who couldn't get to the hospital in time

programme.title: Secrets of Bones
programme.desc: Evolutionary biologist Ben Garrod explores how skeletons have evolved to help animals sense the world around them, revealing why predators like wolves have their eye sockets at the front of their skulls, whereas many prey creatures have a wider fields of vision. The presenter also looks at the hearing abilities of the grey owl, and another animal's flexible nose

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: Sam Neill narrates a documentary examining the wildlife of the island chain, which has been left to its own devices for 80 million years - with surprising consequences. The opening edition features New Zealand's weirdest and most ancient species, including dinosaur-like reptiles, insects that have become giants, and flightless birds that behave like badgers, while the people who settled developed their own unique culture, and all must battle the natural forces that shape the island nation

programme.desc: Tim and Shane navigate their way through ports and islands on the west coast of Scotland, but the misty weather affords them little time for sight-seeing. They then sail the Princess Matilda along the Caledonian Canal to the east coast, where they search for a place to moor their barge for the winter

programme.title: The Lost City of Sanxingdui
programme.desc: A look at one of the most important archaeological discovery of the 20th-century - an ancient city in the mountains of Sichuan, China, which was consigned to oblivion until the chance discovery of a jade object in 1927. Since that first find, over 10,000 artefacts made of gold, jade, ivory and bronze have been unearthed, buried by the inhabitants in sacrificial pits before they left the city about 3,000 years ago

programme.title: The Planets
programme.sub-title: A Moment in the Sun: The Terrestrial Planets
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox tells the life story of the solar system, beginning with the development of the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun - Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. They were born at the same time from the same material - yet have lived radically different lives. What immense forces are at play?

programme.title: Janet Suzman Remembers - The Singing Detective
programme.desc: Dame Janet Suzman shares her memories of making The Singing Detective, Dennis Potter's classic drama serial, which is widely regarded as a landmark television moment. She describes the feeling on set for the cast, lead by Michael Gambon, and how each actor fully committed to their roles in order to bring this multi-layered piece of drama to life

programme.title: The Singing Detective
programme.desc: Dennis Potter's surreal 1986 drama, starring Michael Gambon as a struggling pulp-fiction novelist who begins to mentally assume the role of one of his characters while confined to a hospital bed. However, while he drifts in and out of his fantasy world, he is also confronted by disturbing visions from his childhood. With Patrick Malahide, Joanne Whalley and Imelda Staunton

programme.title: The Singing Detective
programme.desc: Marlow clashes with Dr Gibbon, a hospital psychiatrist who has read one of his novels and thinks he can get to the root of his problems. Meanwhile, in the novel playing out inside his head, the mysterious Binney finds himself in peril. Dennis Potter's darkly surreal 1986 drama, starring Michael Gambon, Bill Paterson and Janet Suzman

programme.desc: Mankind's fascination with the frozen continent of Antarctica, from the early 20th-century race to be the first to reach the South Pole to modern scientific research into the region's geological properties. The programme reveals the story behind the photographs taken by Herbert Ponting on Captain Robert Falcon Scott's ill-fated 1912 polar expedition, explores the South Pole's role in famous literature by HP Lovecraft and Samuel Taylor Coleridge, and examines the continent's complicated political history. With contributions by Ranulph Fiennes, Sara Wheeler and Francis Spufford

programme.desc: Michael Portillo travels through Bohemia and Bavaria, beginning by exploring the art nouveau architecture of Czech Republic capital Prague. Crossing the border into Germany, Michael encounters a fire-breathing dragon in Furth-im-Wald, and learns about an early 20th-century pioneer who laid the foundations for Munich's pre-eminence in science and technology

Heading to Bilbao, he explores the industrial ties between France and Spain and learns to cook a traditional Basque dish

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo ventures once more on to the European rail network to retrace journeys featured in George Bradshaw's 1913 publication Continental Guide, beginning by travelling through Russia. He starts in the industrial city of Tula, before visiting Leo Tolstoy's former home of Yasnaya Polyana and learning how the author's life and works were intertwined with the railways. Michael then boards the train that runs from the Caspian Sea to Moscow, where he performs an important role in a dramatic opera at the Bolshoi Theatre, before exploring the beauty and history of St Petersburg and riding on the first railway ever built in Russia

programme.title: Shetland
programme.desc: Once Perez and his team determine who assaulted Kelly Paterson, a new light is shone on the murder of Michael Thompson - bringing a shocking revelation. Back in Shetland, witness Leanne struggles to deal with the emotional aftermath of being shot, while Perez is troubled to discover that Michael's witness protection handler Asha was in Lerwick on the day the e-mail was sent. As investigators dig deeper into Asha's past, they discover a connection to one of McCall's team and face a race against time to stop the killer from striking again

programme.title: Judge Rinder's Crime Stories
programme.desc: Barrister Robert Rinder examines the murder of Julie Archer by her brother Stephen, who set fire to her in her Greater Manchester home in 2016. Police had their chief suspect almost immediately, but Stephen went on the run, posing an enormous danger to the public at large

programme.title: Heartbeat
programme.desc: A woman is admitted to hospital after a series of burglaries, and Nick and Jo start planning their life together. Greengrass and Bernie try their hand at modern art. Rural police drama, starring Nick Berry and Bill Maynard

programme.title: Endeavour
programme.desc: The detective is assigned to investigate when a chocolate factory owner is murdered during a fox hunt. The case leads him to the sleepy Oxfordshire village of Chigton Green, and is soon complicated by the fatal shooting of a local couple with an apparent connection to the first victim. Endeavour uncovers a vicious campaign of gossip and rumour, and meets a local woman who inspires him to consider his future

programme.title: Posh Pawn
programme.desc: High-end pawnbroker James tries to make an £85,000 deal on a modified sports car, while designer handbag expert Claudia heads to Germany to value a large collection of bags owned by a former New York socialite. A female bodybuilder wants to sell jewellery so she can fund her new hobby, and a golf fanatic brings in a case of vintage wine

programme.title: Heathrow: Britain's Busiest Airport
programme.desc: The Red Arrows fly over the airport during the Queen's Jubilee celebrations, but Passenger Experience Manager Suki has to wake a passenger and get him onboard a flight to Toronto. Also racing to catch their flight are a mother and daughter flying to South Africa to attend a close family relative's funeral. Emotions run high as time ticks away without the correct paperwork, so it's down to Passenger Experience Manager Harry to come to the rescue - but is it already too late?

programme.title: Hairy Bikers: Route 66
programme.desc: Dave Myers and Si King embark on a 2,000-mile journey along the famous American road, taking them through eight different states, each with their own history, flavours and people. They begin by learning about Chicago's meatpacking industry, before moving on to small-town American, where they spend time with the Amish community, cooking together and learning about their different way of life. Their first leg ends in St Louis, where they try 'concrete custard' - a treat so rich and thick it has to be served upside down

programme.title: Heartbeat
programme.desc: Ventress's determination to protect a widow's home from a gang of louts becomes an all-consuming obsession, while Greengrass gets his fingers burnt attempting to break into the fish and chip industry, little realising what a competitive business it is. Rural drama, starring William Simons and Bill Maynard

programme.title: Hotel Benidorm: Fun-Loving Brits in the Sun
programme.desc: Documentary following life at the Spanish Rio Park hotel and the holiday-makers to whom they cater. The first edition sees the staff ready to welcome thousands of Brits, but no sooner have they started than there is a problem when the lifts break down and they race to get them repaired

programme.title: Paddington Station 24/7
programme.desc: Mobile operations manager Jane is called to Burnham, Buckinghamshire, where a van has struck a bridge, and it is up to her to assess whether any significant damage has been caused to the railway line that runs over it. When a train breaks down on platform 15 of Reading station, staff are under pressure to identify and rectify the issue as quickly as possible to avoid any widespread delays, but fixing a fault with the brakes proves to be very complex

programme.title: Emmerdale
programme.desc: Joe puts a new plot into motion, Vinny is in court and Kim is pulled over by the police

programme.title: Coronation Street
programme.desc: Brody and Bernie support Kit as his treatment begins, Debbie feels scrutinised by Ronnie and Jake accuses Gary of misplaced loyalty. Leanne and Idris have a bone to pick with Nick

programme.title: The Royal
programme.desc: Tragedy strikes at the Royal v Ashfordly General rugby match, as Cheriton dives to score a try, only to be pounced on by opponents. It soon emerges that his injuries are serious, and Ormerod rushes to help his colleague - but his efforts prove futile and Cheriton dies at the scene. Meanwhile, Alun is involved in a road accident caused by a man who recently suffered a stroke, and student nurse Samantha Beaumont fails to impress Matron and Sister Brigid by putting pink sheets on the ward's beds. Medical drama, starring Julian Ovenden, Robert Daws, Andy Wear, Stuart Wade, Anna Madeley, Wendy Craig and Linda Armstrong

programme.title: Agatha Christie's Poirot
programme.desc: The sleuth falls victim to depression after failing to prevent the murder of a society girl by notorious art thief Marrascaud. His confidence shattered, Poirot eventually returns to work when a lonely chauffeur begs him to find his missing soulmate, the maid of a famous Russian dancer. The investigation takes him to the Swiss Alps, where, against all odds, he stumbles upon a hotel thought to be Marrascaud's hideout - leading to a very personal showdown. The penultimate episode of the long-running detective drama, starring David Suchet, with Simon Callow, Orla Brady, Patrick Ryecart, Nigel Lindsay, Morven Christie, Tom Austen and Rupert Evans

programme.title: Heartbeat
programme.desc: Greengrass befriends a travelling musician (guest star Gary Barlow) who spreads a little disharmony in Aidensfield, while Jackie's parents drop in unexpectedly, casting a shadow over her relationship with Mike - and all at once domestic bliss becomes a thing of the past in the Bradley household. With Bill Maynard, Jason Durr and Fiona Dolman

programme.title: Vera
programme.desc: A murder at a remote cottage in Northumberland takes DCI Vera Stanhope back to a place full of childhood memories and reminds her of an unsolved case from earlier in her career.
